title: AVO Sub-final(B274)
description: Avionics Sub-Final examination questions with three choices.

questions.question: What is the advantage of continuous loop over spot detector?
options: To detect only one specific point
questions.explanation: A continuous loop sensing system can monitor the entire protected area, whereas a spot detector checks only a particular location.

questions.question: What can cause an intermittent alarm?
questions.explanation: A frayed or damaged wire can create an intermittent electrical condition, which may cause an alarm to appear and disappear.

questions.question: A 40 Ah battery rated at a 10-hour rate can supply approximately how much current?
questions.explanation: A 40 Ah battery on a 10-hour rate supplies 40 ÷ 10 = 4 A for the rated period.

questions.question: Which component of a circuit is responsible for consuming current?
questions.explanation: The load is the part of a circuit that consumes electrical energy and therefore allows current to flow through it.

questions.question: What is the loss associated with repeated magnetization and demagnetization?
questions.explanation: Hysteresis loss occurs because a magnetic material uses energy during repeated magnetization and demagnetization cycles.

questions.question: Which is an example of natural electricity?
questions.explanation: Lightning is a natural electrical discharge produced by charge separation in the atmosphere.

questions.question: What is true about RMS and average value for an AC waveform?
options: Average is always greater than RMS
RMS and average are always equal
questions.explanation: For the waveform considered in the question, the RMS value is greater than the average value, because RMS represents the heating-equivalent magnitude of the AC quantity.

questions.question: What is the function of the multiplier on a voltmeter?
questions.explanation: A multiplier resistor extends the voltage range of a voltmeter so that it can measure a higher voltage than the basic meter movement can handle.

questions.question: What is the brain of the AFCS?
questions.explanation: The AFCS computer processes flight-control inputs and commands, so it acts as the central processing unit or brain of the automatic flight control system.

questions.question: How is Mach trim operated?
questions.explanation: Mach trim is normally controlled automatically so that the aircraft can maintain the required trim as Mach number changes.

questions.question: The angular change in direction of the plane of rotation under the influence of an applied force at a point 90 degrees away in the direction of rotation is called what?
questions.explanation: Precession is the change in the direction of a gyroscope's rotational plane when an applied force acts at right angles to the rotor motion.

questions.question: Where is the drain hole located in the pitot tube?
options: Between the pitot probe and the casing
questions.explanation: The drain arrangement provides a path for moisture to leave the space between the pitot probe and its casing, helping prevent water accumulation.

questions.question: How many accelerometers are there in the INS gyroscope system?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer is two accelerometers in the INS gyroscope arrangement described by the question.

questions.question: What do the abbreviations CISC and RISC stand for?
options: Computer Input Signal Circuit and Radio Interface Signal Circuit
Complex Instruction Set Computing and Reduced Instruction Set Computing
Central Integrated System Control and Remote Instrument System Control
questions.explanation: CISC means Complex Instruction Set Computing, while RISC means Reduced Instruction Set Computing; the names describe different processor instruction-set approaches.

questions.question: What is the function of the accumulator register?
questions.explanation: The accumulator is a processor register used to hold intermediate data and results produced during arithmetic and logic operations by the ALU.

questions.question: Which of the following is an input device?
questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device because it allows the user to enter data or commands into a computer.

questions.question: Which technology has minimum power dissipation?
questions.explanation: CMOS logic is known for very low static power consumption, making its power dissipation small compared with many other logic technologies.

questions.question: Which one is not a neutralizing electrolyte agent for NiCd batteries?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies sodium bicarbonate as the item that is not a neutralizing electrolyte agent for a NiCd battery condition.

questions.question: Which amplifier class has the highest linearity and low distortion?
questions.explanation: Class A amplifiers conduct for the full cycle and are known for good linearity and low distortion, although they are less efficient.

questions.question: Which service is directly connected to the AC battery?
questions.explanation: Vital services are electrical services that must remain available for essential aircraft operation and are therefore connected to the required battery supply.

questions.question: What is the range of low frequency according to the stated answer?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer gives the low-frequency range as 20 Hz to 100 kHz.

questions.question: Which one is odd?
questions.explanation: A flip-flop is a bistable storage device used to hold one bit of information, unlike combinational devices such as basic adders.

questions.question: What is the function of a PMG?
questions.explanation: A permanent magnet generator provides an initial source of electrical excitation so generator operation can be established.

questions.question: Which one provides a high output voltage?
questions.explanation: A boost arrangement raises the output voltage above the input voltage, so it is associated with obtaining a higher output voltage.

questions.question: MOSFET/JFET are associated with which technology?
questions.explanation: MOSFET and JFET are field-effect transistor devices commonly associated with MOS/CMOS electronic technology in the context of this question.

questions.question: What is the resistance of a PN junction in its conducting condition?
questions.explanation: When a PN junction is forward biased and conducting, its effective resistance is low, allowing significant current to flow.

questions.question: What is the amount of electrical energy that a cell can provide from new condition to the end of its useful voltage on load called?
questions.explanation: Cell capacity is the amount of electrical charge a cell can deliver under specified conditions before its terminal voltage falls to the defined end point.

questions.question: What does an ADC converter determine?
options: The mechanical speed of a motor
questions.explanation: An ADC quantizes an analog signal into digital steps; its resolution determines the smallest change or amount that can be distinguished.

questions.question: Which SCR terminal is used to fire the device?
questions.explanation: The gate terminal of an SCR receives the triggering signal that turns the device on when the required conditions are met.

questions.question: What does a rotary inverter convert?
options: DC directly to mechanical braking force
DC motor input to a three-phase AC generator output
Three-phase AC directly to hydraulic pressure
questions.explanation: A rotary inverter uses a motor to drive a generator, converting DC electrical input into three-phase AC electrical output.

questions.question: In which connection is VL = 1.73 VP?
questions.explanation: In a balanced three-phase star (wye) connection, the line voltage is √3 times the phase voltage, so VL = 1.73 VP.

questions.question: What does the FCC control in relation to the control surface?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies forward as the direction associated with the FCC-to-control-surface relationship in this question.

questions.question: Which one is NOT an advantage of crimping?
questions.explanation: Weak strength is not an advantage of crimping; a properly made crimp should provide a strong and reliable electrical and mechanical connection.

questions.question: Which term describes a system that is not linear?
questions.explanation: A non-linear system does not maintain a directly proportional relationship between input and output, so it is described as non-linear.

questions.question: What does a motor-driven impeller transmit?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the transmitted quantity as electrical; the motor-driven impeller is associated with transferring the drive into the instrument system.

questions.question: What is the function of gears in an instrument?
options: Increase or decrease rotor motion and change straight motion to curved motion
questions.explanation: Instrument gears can change the amount of movement, increase or decrease rotation, and convert one type of mechanical motion into the movement needed by the indication mechanism.

questions.question: What is the process of mixing two frequencies in a non-linear device called?
questions.explanation: Heterodyning is the process of combining frequencies in a non-linear device to produce new frequency components, including sum and difference frequencies.

questions.question: Which display remains true if the bank angle does not exceed 30 degrees?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the radio altimeter for this question; a radio altimeter provides altitude information by measuring the aircraft's height above the surface using radio signals.

questions.question: Where is an AC generator driven by a GTE found?
questions.explanation: A gas-turbine engine can drive the aircraft AC generator through the engine accessory drive section.

questions.question: What is the depth of penetration of current into a conductor called?
questions.explanation: Skin depth is the distance into a conductor over which an alternating current decreases significantly from its surface value because of the skin effect.

questions.question: What is below the Application layer in the OSI model?
questions.explanation: In the OSI model, the Presentation layer is directly below the Application layer and is responsible for functions such as data representation and format conversion.

questions.question: What does the receiver of an optical fiber system do?
options: Converts optical signals to electrical signals
Converts RF signals to fuel pressure
Converts electrical signals to hydraulic pressure
questions.explanation: An optical receiver detects the incoming light signal and converts it into an electrical signal that can be processed by the receiving equipment.

questions.question: Which is NOT a purpose of an HF controller?
questions.explanation: According to the supplied answer, increasing or decreasing volume is not considered a purpose of the HF controller in this question.

questions.question: What is a function of weather radar?
questions.explanation: Weather radar is used to detect and display weather activity ahead of the aircraft, including areas of precipitation and associated turbulence.

questions.question: Which equipment generates the carrier frequency and performs modulation and demodulation for RF/MF communication?
questions.explanation: An HF transceiver provides the transmit and receive functions for HF communication, including generation, modulation and demodulation of the RF communication signal.

questions.question: Which is NOT a function of GPWS?
questions.explanation: GPWS provides warnings related to unsafe proximity to terrain and other hazardous flight conditions; excessive electrical-load protection is not a GPWS function.

questions.question: Which of the following uses three-phase power?
questions.explanation: Landing-gear systems can use three-phase electrical power for their actuators or associated drive equipment in the aircraft system described.

questions.question: What is the phase difference associated with an inductive and capacitive motor arrangement?
questions.explanation: A split-phase arrangement uses phase displacement between winding currents to create the required rotating magnetic field for motor operation.

questions.question: Why is a series-wound motor preferred over a shunt-wound motor for high starting loads?
questions.explanation: A series-wound motor develops high starting torque because the field winding carries the same high starting current as the armature.

questions.question: What does the status mode display indicate according to the supplied answer?
questions.explanation: The supplied answer identifies the status mode display as the low display unit for the system described by the question.
